claim: admission_record_problems accepts any Decision Log prose entry as the record's decision_ref, as long as decision_section_sha256 matches that entry's bytes. Nothing checks that the cited entry is the family's own decision, so a record that cites an unrelated entry, another family's entry or DL-077 itself counts as complete. DL-077 defines the record as naming Jared's decision entry for that family and says a mismatched record fails closed. DL-078, the receipt's record_contract and the new spec section all say the cited entry names the family. DL-077 allows no later validator edit, so this has to be fixed in this change.
evidence: Code at f3289d49: 'match = re.fullmatch(r"Plans/Decision_Log\.md#(DL-\d{3})", ...)', then only 'if record.get("decision_section_sha256") != hashlib.sha256(section).hexdigest()'. DL-077 prose: 'Jared's decision entry for that family' and 'fails closed for any family without one, with a malformed or mismatched record'. DL-078 prose: 'The Decision Log entry each such landing adds names the family and is the decision entry its DL-077 admission record cites.' Receipt record_contract.decision_ref: '... the Decision Log entry its landing adds, which names the family'. Spec: 'A complete record names Jared's decision entry for that family'. Probe in the all-PASS counterfactual tree (logs/probe_gaps.log): I re-cited browser.workspace.created's record to DL-041 (the Settings DRY-guard decision, which does not contain the event type), to DL-040 (the compaction decision) and to DL-077, each time with the entry's correct section hash. The family was admitted each time, with no issue reported.
suggested_repair: In admission_record_problems, directly after the decision_section_sha256 comparison, insert: 'named = re.search(rb"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_.])" + re.escape(str(event_type)).encode() + rb"(?![A-Za-z0-9_]|\.[A-Za-z0-9_])", section)' and 'if match.group(1) in ("DL-077", "DL-078") or not named: problems.append("decision_ref_not_for_family")' (proposed/validator-repairs.patch). In the spec, after 'the SHA-256 of its prose section;' add 'the cited entry must name the family's exact event type and cannot be DL-077 or DL-078;'. Add the test test_decision_entry_must_name_the_family (proposed/tests-repairs.patch). All three current records still pass this check: DL-040 names context.compaction.completed, and DL-046 names both Browser families.

claim: The depth check finds the assessment row by event_type alone. It never compares that row's family_id and family_revision with the live registry row. An assessment that graded another family id, or an earlier revision of the family, is therefore accepted as the family's current depth assessment. For example, if a family is re-versioned and only its registry_row_sha256 is re-pinned, the old grades still count. DL-077 requires a current assessment and fails closed on a mismatched record, and it allows no later validator edit.
evidence: Code: 'rows = [r for r in (load_json(full).get("rows") or []) if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("event_type") == event_type]', followed only by the cells checks. Assessment rows and registry rows both carry family_id and family_revision; for example browser.workspace.created has event-family-browser-workspace-created at 1.0.0 in both. Probe E2 (logs/probe_gaps.log): I changed the created row to family_revision 9.9.9 and family_id event-family-something-else and re-pinned the records. The family was admitted with no issue. In the pinned assessment (ba9b84f9 at 3ce6eb882c), all 42 rows match their registry rows, with 0 mismatches, so the repair changes no current result.
suggested_repair: After the 'if len(rows) != 1:' block, insert: 'if (rows[0].get("family_id") != family.get("family_id") or rows[0].get("family_revision") != family.get("family_revision")): problems.append("depth_assessment.family_revision"); return problems' (proposed/validator-repairs.patch). In the spec, after 'whose row for the family has all twelve criteria at PASS', add ', and whose family_id and family_revision equal the live registry row'. Add the test test_depth_row_must_grade_the_registered_family_revision (proposed/tests-repairs.patch).

claim: For an admitted family, the amendment stops judging depth from its ledger row. That row needed every cell at PASS with a citation under Plans/ (cell_ok_pass). Instead, a criterion now counts when the assessment says status PASS, and no evidence is required. A PASS with no evidence, or with evidence only outside Plans/, is accepted. That is looser than the rule the same family faced before the amendment, and looser than DL-077's statement that the amendment keeps every existing rule.
evidence: Code: 'failing = [f for f in EVIDENCE_FIELDS if not isinstance(cells.get(f), dict) or cells[f].get("status") != "PASS"]'. registered_like now skips post_august_admitted, and cell_ok_pass requires 'cit.startswith("Plans/")'. Probe E3: with the evidence and finding removed from all twelve created cells, the family was admitted. All 335 PASS cells in the pinned assessment carry at least one evidence path under Plans/ (logs/depth42_pass_evidence.txt), so the repair changes no current result.
suggested_repair: After the depth_incomplete check, insert the 'uncited' block from proposed/validator-repairs.patch. It reports 'depth_pass_without_plans_evidence:<criteria>' for any PASS cell whose evidence list has no item whose path starts with 'Plans/'. In the spec, add 'and each PASS cell carries at least one evidence item whose path is under Plans/'. Give the test fixture cells an evidence item, and add test_a_pass_without_plans_evidence_fails_closed (proposed/tests-repairs.patch).

claim:
The 24 tests pass. At function level they cover missing, stale, forged and incomplete records, and the Step 3 chain. But no test runs main(), so none of the amendment's four changes to main() is tested, and several record and receipt checks are untested too. I applied each of the following mutations with the receipt re-pinned, and all 24 tests still passed every time:
- live_august no longer subtracts the admitted families
- blocking_ledger reverted to the whole ledger
- registered_like reverted
- post_august_admission_incomplete removed from depth_blocking
- the post_august_admission_incomplete failure never appended
- the before/after SHA-256 difference check dropped
- the twelve-criteria set check dropped
- duplicate assessment rows accepted
- the file-name check dropped (the uniqueness check masks it)
- the lander_task and record_schema_id receipt checks dropped
evidence: logs/mutation.log: M1, M3, M4, M6, M7, M8, M9, M10, M12, M16, M17, M18 and M19 left all 24 tests passing; M2, M5, M11, M13, M14 and M15 were caught. The existing tests call validate_post_august_admissions and validate_holding_bucket directly and never call main().
suggested_repair:
Add the nine tests in proposed/tests-repairs.patch, which gives 33 tests. Three of them run main() with RECEIPT_DIR pointed at the temporary root:
- With complete records: no unexpected_august_set, no post_august_admission_incomplete, and none of the three families in the evidence-gap or registered-depth samples.
- With one incomplete record: that family appears in unexpected_august_set and in the evidence-gap sample, and post_august_admission_incomplete is present.
- With a stray record: the stray-record issue is reported.
With the V-01 to V-03 repairs all 33 pass. The mutation run then catches everything except three low-value cases: the depth_blocking entry, the '..' path check and the redundant DL-077 token check (logs/mutation-repaired.log).

claim: The schema note says a completely recorded family 'is judged by that record, not by its row here', and both documents say its row 'no longer counts as blocking'. The code removes the row from only five places: the owner-veto, evidence-gap, unresolved and quarantine blocking checks, and registered depth. The provisional, evidence-shape, ADMIT_CANDIDATE, inference, holding and denominator-membership checks still read the row, and a provisional flag on it still blocks. The spec also says a complete record names Jared's decision entry for that family, which the code does not check (V-01).
evidence:
Code at f3289d49:
- blocking_ledger feeds only owner_veto_blocking, evidence_gap_blocking, unresolved_blocking and quarantine_blocking.
- 'provisional_rows = [r for r in ledger if r.get("provisional")]' still runs over the whole ledger.

Every other row check (evidence shape, provisional, ADMIT_CANDIDATE, inference, holding and denominator membership) still applies to it.'

claim:
Landing order. The records pin reports/event-authority-20260911/step-08-depth42-assessment-20260924.json, which exists only on plans/ea-step08-depth42-20260924. So this branch must land after depth42, and only while that file still hashes to the pinned value. The branches share no path and merge cleanly. On main plus this branch alone, the three families fail with depth_assessment.sha256 instead of their real gaps. Two things also order the landing:
- The validator requires lander_task to equal the author, so only claude-opus-5.5:dl039-steps-8-9-20260924 can land this truthfully.
- After landing, the records and the receipt pin the three registry rows, the DL-040, DL-046 and DL-077 prose sections, and the assessment bytes. Any later change to one of them has to re-pin in the same landing, or the check fails closed.
evidence: Run G (5cd53e7bc2 without depth42): the three issues are 'depth_assessment.sha256'. Run F (with the 3ce6eb882c assessment, ba9b84f9): the issues are the three depth_incomplete lists. There is no path overlap between ac9c0ad2e4..3ce6eb882c and ac9c0ad2e4..5cd53e7bc2. The DL-040, DL-046 and DL-077 section hashes are identical on main and at 3ce6eb882c; only DL-078 changes. The validator checks 'receipt.get("lander_task") != POST_AUGUST_AUTHOR'. The other open branch that touches the registry, origin/fix/packet-gap-closure-20260911-landing-dc5, is a stale 2026-09-11 bulk-Browser branch and does not order this one.
suggested_repair: Land only after plans/ea-step08-depth42-20260924 is on main, with the assessment still at SHA-256 ba9b84f99e0e0761a8b435a16602d4c88d14589ef273f789fd5b92bdbd5849fd. Otherwise re-pin the three records first. Then rebase, and before pushing main rerun the validator (6 failures, with the three depth_incomplete issues) and the tests. The author task claude-opus-5.5:dl039-steps-8-9-20260924 must do the landing itself. If anyone else has to land it, stop and ask, because correcting lander_task would take another validator edit. Every DL-078 registration landing must add its family's record in the same landing.

claim: In Step 3, each applied holding row pins the Step 3 receipt's SHA-256, so editing that receipt breaks 54 ledger rows. Nothing pins the DL-077 receipt. The holding check now accepts whatever validator bytes the receipt's validator_after_sha256 names, so a third, unauthorized validator edit needs only that one field changed. DL-077 does not require more, and git history still shows such an edit, so this is hardening, not a defect.
evidence: validate_holding_bucket now compares the Step 3 pin with holding_validator_pin(), which returns the DL-077 receipt's validator_before_sha256 after checking that receipt's validator_after_sha256 against the current file. The admission records carry no implementation_receipt_sha256. Step 3's rows carry 'implementation_receipt_sha256' (INDIVIDUAL_DISPOSITION_SCHEMA.md).
suggested_repair: Optional, in this change only: add "implementation_receipt_sha256" (the DL-077 receipt's SHA-256) to each record and to the record_contract. In admission_record_problems, require it to equal sha256_file(REPO / POST_AUGUST_RECEIPT).

claim: The validator enforces 'current' only through the pinned hashes. Nothing ties the assessment's own registry block (2026-09-11.2, 0be54418...) to the live registry. While the family's registry row is unchanged, an assessment made against an older registry is accepted. Requiring equality would force a new assessment for every admitted family at every Step 9 registration. That is a policy choice DL-077 leaves open, not a defect.
evidence: Probe E4 (logs/probe_gaps.log): I set the assessment's registry block to the 2026-08-27.1 registry (39 families) and re-pinned the records. All three families were still admitted.
suggested_repair: Record this as an open question for the coordinator: should 'current' also mean that the assessment's registry.sha256 equals the live registry's? Make no change unless the coordinator decides so.
